title: Principality of Hungary
capsule: The Principality of Hungary (Magyar Fejedelemség) was the earliest Hungarian state, established in the Carpathian Basin following the Magyar conquest led by Grand Prince Árpád around 895, displacing the Moravians and Bulgars from the Pannonian plain. Magyar cavalry raided deep into France, Italy, and the Byzantine Empire throughout the early 10th century until the decisive defeat at the Battle of Lechfeld by Otto I in 955 ended the raiding era and reoriented Hungary toward sedentary statehood. Grand Prince Géza (r. c. 972–997) began systematic Christianization, and his son Stephen I (István) received a papal crown in 1000 or 1001, formally converting the principality into the Christian Kingdom of Hungary.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Principality's core Pannonian territory is well documented; precise boundaries toward Moravia, Bohemia, and Bulgaria were fluid and are reconstructed from Byzantine, Frankish, and Hungarian chronicle sources with moderate confidence.
